sentences.text: What if the most beautiful angel ever painted is looking at you with pure hatred?
This is The Fallen Angel, painted by Alexandre Cabanel in 1847.
A young angel lies on a rock, his wings folded under him, while other angels fly above.
There is a tear in it.
And he is staring straight at you.
According to the old story of the fall, God threw this angel out of heaven, and he became the Devil.
A fallen angel should look broken.
But Cabanel painted him enraged, not sorry.
The tear says he is grieving, yet the eye says something else.
As if grief is turning into hatred while you watch.
Maybe this is the last second he is still an angel.
So when his eye meets yours, is he asking for pity, or promising revenge?

meta.title: The most beautiful angel ever painted is not sorry
meta.description: The Fallen Angel (L'Ange déchu) was painted by Alexandre Cabanel in 1847, when he was 24, at the Villa Médicis in Rome. It shows the Devil just after his fall from Heaven: tears in his eyes, glaring out from behind his arm. Musée Fabre, Montpellier.
meta.question: Asking for pity, or promising revenge?

sources.claim: Painted in 1847 when the artist was 24; depicts the Devil after his fall from Heaven; an angel expelled from heaven by God, enraged, hands crossed, tears running from his eyes; glares out angrily from behind his arm; angels fly in the sky above; Musée Fabre, Montpellier
